solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chicken brood's left a little late in bed of shells and gravel

indicators.note: the letter for left is set down slightly later in the word than where it began, one place further along

parts.note: a clutch is a set of eggs or chicks hatched together
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A hen's chicks have been left a little late in a nest made of shells and grit.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the L out of CLUTCH and put it back one letter later, after the U, to get CULTCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Cultch is the mass of old shells, stones and grit spread on an oyster bed for spat to settle on.

clue.text: Soccer's authority is in referee's colourful reprimand for Blues

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it, wrapped by the second

parts.note: a referee shows a yellow or red card
the FA is the Football Association, English soccer's governing body

explanation.surface: The football association gets mixed up in a referee showing a yellow card.
explanation.walkthrough: Blues looks like a team in the football surface, but it means low spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafard is a French-derived word for depression or a fit of melancholy, which is what having the blues means.

clue.text: Shrub or flip's contents: blow and liquor

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what lies inside it, its letters minus the outer ones

parts.note: the inner pair of letters of the word flip
a gust is a blow of wind
rum is a spirit, a liquor

explanation.surface: A flip is a mixed drink, and its contents here sound like a stiff blow plus rum.
explanation.walkthrough: A flip is a hot drink of beer or spirit with egg and sugar, which makes the surface read as a recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Ligustrum is the botanical genus name for privet, a common hedging shrub.

clue.text: Hooded striker's supporter arises as spiritual successor for Celtic

parts.note: a cobra spreads its hood before it strikes; its first two letters stay put

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports, and it is the snake's last three letters

explanation.surface: A footballer in a hood has a fan who rises to become heir to Celtic.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the supporter inside the snake's name rises; the rest stays where it is. Celtic is the Glasgow football club in the surface but the ancient Celtic church in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarb in the early Irish and Celtic church was the successor of a founding saint as abbot, an ecclesiastical heir.

clue.text: Psalm for Mass's one in stony defence of Boers

indicators.note: one thing for another means it is put in place of it, swapped in

parts.note: mass in the sense of bulk or magnitude
the Roman numeral for one, here the letter being replaced
psalms are sung as a chant

explanation.surface: A psalm replaces the Mass in a church set inside a stone fort of the Boers.
explanation.walkthrough: Mass and Psalm look liturgical, but Mass here is a measure of bulk. The Boers were Dutch-descended settlers in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A schantze was a breastwork of piled stones, a small field fortification built by Boer fighters in South Africa.

clue.text: Digestive processes disrupted in stomach if icy

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the fourteen letters of these four words, taken as written

explanation.surface: Digestion goes wrong in the stomach if you eat or drink something icy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chymification is the stage of digestion in which food in the stomach is turned into chyme, a pulpy acid fluid.

clue.text: Catch rain after treatment of wool-sorter's disease

indicators.note: treatment works on material and changes its form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the nine letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A wool-sorter catches the rain, and after treatment is still sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Wool-sorter's disease is the old trade name for anthrax caught from infected fleeces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracic is the adjective relating to anthrax, an infection historically common among people handling raw wool.

clue.text: In retrospect, only time reveals ultimate purpose

indicators.note: looking in retrospect is looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Looking back, only the passing of time shows what something was really for.
explanation.definitionFit: Telos is the Greek philosophical term for an end or goal, the final aim toward which a thing tends.

clue.text: Slacker to board coach ahead of waiting line, with 40 per cent off

indicators.note: taking forty per cent off a five-letter word removes two of its letters

parts.note: to embus is to get on a bus or coach
a queue is a line of people waiting

explanation.surface: A lazy person boards the coach ahead of the people waiting in line, with a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEUE loses its last two letters to leave QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An embusqué is a shirker, originally someone who dodged frontline military service by taking a safe job.

clue.text: Smallest state twice catching very American smuggler involves scene that can make you smile

indicators.note: catching something means holding it between, so the first part wraps round the second

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state, written twice
so means very, as in so good
US is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: to involve is to enfold or wrap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a mule is someone who smuggles drugs across a border
sc is the abbreviation for scene in a play

explanation.surface: A tiny state catches an American smuggler twice, and the scene is enough to make you grin.
explanation.walkthrough: Rhode Island is the smallest US state by area, and a mule is slang for a drug courier.
explanation.definitionFit: The risorius is a narrow facial muscle that pulls the corners of the mouth sideways, producing a grin.

clue.text: Extreme conservative confusion beginning to ruin friendship

parts.note: being in a fog is being confused

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of ruin
amity is friendly relations

explanation.surface: An extremely conservative attitude causes confusion that begins to ruin a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: Fogramity means old-fogeyism, or a person who is an old fogey, someone stubbornly behind the times.

clue.text: Of two-party arrangements, just over half repelled fundamentalist

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the letters run backwards
keeping only a little more than half a word means cutting the rest away

parts.note: bilateral describes arrangements made between two parties

explanation.surface: A two-party deal is just over half done when a fundamentalist pushes it back.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep the first five of BILATERAL's nine letters, BILAT, and turn them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A Talib is a member of the Taliban, the Islamist movement known for its hardline religious rule.

clue.text: Point out ring from radials

indicators.note: out here means taken away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
to dial is to ring on the telephone

explanation.surface: Point out the ring on a set of radial tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DIAL from the middle of RADIALS leaves RAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ras is a headland or cape, from the Arabic for head, so a geographical point of land.

clue.text: Cause of smell that's strong or faint, recalled between siblings familiarly

indicators.note: something between two others is placed inside them

parts.note: bro and sis are the familiar forms of brother and sister
taken as written

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the words are read backwards

parts.note: dim means faint, as in a dim light

explanation.surface: Something gives off a smell that is either strong or faint, as brother and sister remember it.
explanation.walkthrough: Strong looks like it belongs with or faint as a pair of choices, but it ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bromidrosis is a medical term for sweat that smells foul, the source of strong body odour.

clue.text: Man turns on doctor who's closing passages in temple

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: the closing of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of who

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man turns on a doctor who is shutting up shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Man is the Isle of Man, not a person. In an across clue, A on B puts A after B.
explanation.definitionFit: Dromoi is the plural of dromos, the long entrance corridor leading into an ancient Greek temple or tomb.

clue.text: In greatest quantity, receiving a thousand cases of often fizzy grape syrup

indicators.note: a thing receiving another takes it inside itself

parts.note: most means the greatest amount
K stands for a thousand

indicators.note: the cases of words are their outer letters, the shells around them

parts.note: the first and last letters of often
the first and last letters of fizzy

explanation.surface: A drink receives huge amounts of something that is often fizzy, a thousand cases of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The thousand and both pairs of outer letters all sit together inside the first word, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Moskonfyt is a South African syrup made by boiling down unfermented grape juice, a thick sweet must.

clue.text: Perhaps a local character taking care of whitefish

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within

parts.note: a local is a pub, and an inn is one kind
c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
nu is a Greek letter, a character

explanation.surface: A well-known local figure looks after some whitefish.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain your local is the pub you usually drink at; Perhaps signals that an inn is one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The inconnu is a large predatory whitefish of Arctic rivers, its French name meaning the unknown one.

clue.text: To add difficulty, see about withdrawing Scottish legal charter

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the string runs backwards

parts.note: to sum is to add up
ado means fuss or trouble, as in without further ado
v is short for vide, Latin for see
on means about, as in a talk on birds

explanation.surface: A lawyer says, to add a complication, look at withdrawing the Scottish charter.
explanation.definitionFit: A novodamus is a charter in Scots law that grants something anew, renewing or correcting an earlier grant.

clue.text: Sign covering papers held by commander-in-chief protected by shell

indicators.note: a thing covering another lies over and around it

parts.note: C-in-C, the usual abbreviation for commander-in-chief

indicators.note: being held by something means sitting inside its grip

parts.note: Leo is a sign of the zodiac
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: A sign covers papers that the commander-in-chief is holding.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the papers go inside the sign, and the sign goes inside the commander's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleidoic egg is enclosed in a shell that seals it off from the outside, like those of birds and reptiles.

clue.text: Ferrari's agreed to stop luxury cars being abnormally thirsty?

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, sitting in the gap in its middle

parts.note: limos are limousines
si is Italian for yes, as an Italian such as Ferrari would agree

explanation.surface: Ferrari has agreed to halt production of luxury cars that guzzle fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ferrari stands for any Italian speaker. The question mark flags a loose definition: limosis is strictly a morbid hunger.
explanation.definitionFit: Limosis is an abnormal, insatiable craving, a disordered appetite, so a looser way to describe it is morbid thirst.

clue.text: Brewer's product protecting business against recession

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it as a shield

parts.note: a brewer makes ale
Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
v is short for versus, meaning against

explanation.surface: A brewery's output keeps a company safe during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: The economic sense of recession is a decoy; the definition means a recess in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recess, a part of a room set back from the main wall, so recession in its spatial sense.

clue.text: Former unenlightened batter is off beam for breaking down doors

indicators.note: something that is off has gone away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: a battering ram is a heavy beam used to break in
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: A former ignorant batsman leaves, beam in hand, for breaking down doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Take BATTER from the front of BATTERING RAM. Batter looks like a cricketer or a pancake mix but is just letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingram is an obsolete word for ignorant, so it describes someone unlearned in a sense no longer in use.

clue.text: Flexible stone's desirable quality on both sides of a short pillar by end of arcade

indicators.note: something on both sides of another flanks it, enclosing it

parts.note: it is sex appeal, used once on each side

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, losing the final letter

parts.note: taken as written
a column is a pillar

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of arcade

explanation.surface: A flexible stone has a desirable look on either side of a stubby pillar beside an arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: It, meaning sex appeal, is used twice, once on each side. Short trims the pillar by its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Itacolumite is a sandstone with interlocking grains that lets thin slabs bend, hence a stone that flexes.

clue.text: Hopelessness in breakdown of society's physical structure, at being estranged

indicators.note: estranged means removed or separated, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: anatomy is the structure of the body
taken as written, the part removed

explanation.surface: Despair runs through society as its body falls apart and people grow estranged.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove AT from ANATOMY to leave ANOMY.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomy, or anomie, is a sociological term for the despair and lack of purpose felt when social norms collapse.

clue.text: Erotic feeling when stripping all curvy characters outside for reproductive stuff

indicators.note: stripping something takes it off, so those letters go
putting letters outside means sending them away from the word

parts.note: sexiness is sexual allure or erotic feeling
S is the curvy letter, and all three are removed

explanation.surface: Erotic feeling arises when a curvy figure strips for some reproductive purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: Every S is dropped from SEXINESS, leaving EXINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The exine is the tough outer wall of a pollen grain or spore, part of a plant's reproductive material.

clue.text: Marker buoy or tub, locally and at sea

parts.note: first meaning: a small buoy used to mark a position at sea
second meaning: a dialect word for a small tub or truck in a mine

indicators.note: something at sea is lost and confused, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A buoy marks a spot, or a tub floats about locally out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions and an anagram of AND all lead to the same three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dan is a small buoy used by fishermen to mark nets, and in dialect also a small tub or mine cart.

clue.text: Pared-down Damnation of Faust with intermissions

indicators.note: pared down means trimmed at both ends, leaving only a piece from inside the phrase

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of the first word, all of the middle one and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A cut-down performance of Berlioz's opera The Damnation of Faust, given with intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on-off happens intermittently, stopping and starting with gaps between spells of activity.

clue.text: One validates constant, endless burning with instant resistance

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
on fire means burning
a mo is a moment, an instant
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Someone confirms a constant burning that comes with instant resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: ON FIRE loses its E to give ONFIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A confirmor is a person who confirms, ratifying or affirming that something is valid.

clue.text: I suggest we turned across river, chasing evasive knave

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so this part comes later in the word

parts.note: coy means unwilling to give a straight answer

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the letters read backwards
lying across something means spanning it, so one part sits over and around the other

parts.note: let's is how one proposes doing something together
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Someone proposes turning across the river to pursue a cagey rogue.
explanation.walkthrough: I suggest we is the setter's way of saying let us, as in let's go.
explanation.definitionFit: Coystrel is an archaic word for a base fellow or rascal, the same as a knave.

clue.text: Oil producer's to appear to bury unpublished text

indicators.note: burying something puts it deep inside another thing

parts.note: to seem is to appear
MS is manuscript, a text not yet published

explanation.surface: An oil company is set to show up and bury a document that was never released.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s after Oil producer means is.
explanation.definitionFit: Semsem is another name for sesame, the plant whose seeds are pressed for sesame oil.
